purpose: Prioritize Mythical's first commercial distribution candidates for evidence gathering without treating public research as qualification, demand, revenue, or outreach permission.

model.internalRankMeaning: Sequence for the next reversible evidence-gathering step only; not market attractiveness, revenue probability, or partner endorsement.

portfolioRecommendation: Run one Game Development portal-build feasibility spike with OP-001 as the packaging baseline and OP-002 through OP-004 as requirement test cases; do not contact, create accounts, accept terms, integrate SDKs, upload builds, forecast revenue, or change pipeline stage.

assessments.valueHypothesis: A low-coupling browser packaging and positioning test may provide useful distribution learning before SDK-heavy channels.
assessments.decisionServed: Can one portable browser build satisfy a simple hosted-page path without contaminating the canonical game?

audienceFit.rationale: General indie/browser discovery is plausible, but Mythical audience fit has no accepted customer evidence.

productFit.rationale: HTML browser packaging is supported, while current root-absolute paths and iframe behavior remain untested.

trustSafety.rationale: Lower SDK coupling is attractive, but account, comments, moderation, terms, privacy, and age treatment remain unreviewed.

strategicLearning.rationale: The packaging spike can answer portability and listing-positioning questions reusable across later portals.

reachQuality.rationale: No Mythical-specific qualified reach or conversion evidence exists.

economicPotential.rationale: Donations, fees, tax, delivery cost, and willingness to support are unverified.

controlRights.rationale: A simple listing appears reversible, but current terms and asset rights need professional review.

integrationEffort.rationale: Portable paths, ZIP layout, iframe, CSP/CORS, functions, and persistence need one bounded spike.

operationalLoad.rationale: Listing updates, support, comments, incident handling, and owner capacity are unassigned.

reversibility.rationale: A company-controlled isolated package can be withdrawn without making it the canonical build.

assessments.internalNextAction: Use OP-001 as the baseline case in GDH-005; produce technical evidence only and keep the opportunity at researched.

assessments.valueHypothesis: An adult/general indie community pilot may provide qualitative feedback after portable packaging and moderation controls exist.
assessments.decisionServed: Can the portable package and adult-directed moderation model support useful community feedback without identity or social API integration?

audienceFit.rationale: Adult/general indie feedback may be useful, but audience and trust fit are unvalidated.

productFit.rationale: HTML ZIP and iframe support are relevant, while compatibility is untested.

trustSafety.rationale: Community features create moderation and contact risks even with optional identity APIs disabled.

strategicLearning.rationale: A bounded community pilot could test comprehension and first-session response after adult research.

reachQuality.rationale: No qualified Mythical reach or response evidence exists.

economicPotential.rationale: Revenue, fees, support cost, and commercial outcomes are unverified.

controlRights.rationale: Ownership rules appear relevant, but terms, rights, removal, and derivative treatment require review.

integrationEffort.rationale: Portable iframe packaging is needed; identity, save, scoreboard, and social APIs remain out of scope.

operationalLoad.rationale: Community monitoring, moderation, support, updates, and incident response have no named owner.

reversibility.rationale: An isolated no-social-API package could be removed if terms and export/removal controls are acceptable.

assessments.internalNextAction: Evaluate only after OP-001 packaging evidence and a named moderation/support owner; keep platform identity and social APIs off.

assessments.valueHypothesis: A reviewed browser-platform launch could produce distribution and product learning if first-session, SDK, advertising, age, privacy, and support boundaries are acceptable.
assessments.decisionServed: Do platform reach and feedback justify the SDK, advertising, data, audience, mobile, and operational obligations?

audienceFit.rationale: A browser-games audience is relevant, but Mythical's adult/general positioning and audience fit remain unvalidated.

productFit.rationale: Browser delivery fits, while controls, text density, mobile behavior, onboarding, and quality need portal QA.

trustSafety.rationale: SDK, advertising, consent, identity, 13+ audience, and data-flow implications require explicit review.

strategicLearning.rationale: A platform evaluation could answer first-session and broader browser-distribution questions.

reachQuality.rationale: No Mythical-specific qualified reach, play quality, or audience-overlap evidence exists.

economicPotential.rationale: Revenue share, ads, fees, payout, tax, support cost, and unit economics are unverified.

controlRights.rationale: Launch, SDK, data, advertising, update, removal, and content terms need review.

integrationEffort.rationale: Portal build, onboarding, mobile QA, and possible SDK features add material integration work.

operationalLoad.rationale: Updates, support, moderation, data incidents, reporting, and platform response have no owner or cost baseline.

reversibility.rationale: An isolated adapter can help, but SDK/data/ad and platform obligations may reduce reversibility.

assessments.internalNextAction: Use the GDH-005 spike to measure portal compatibility; do not evaluate an SDK or submission until adult evidence, privacy/safeguarding, finance, support, and owner gates exist.

assessments.valueHypothesis: A high-quality cross-device portal version may create distribution value only if load, SDK, ads, consent, privacy, assets, and support requirements are compatible with Mythical's trust model.
assessments.decisionServed: Can Mythical meet the technical and policy bar without compromising experience, privacy, safety, economics, or canonical-build control?

audienceFit.rationale: Broad web-game discovery is plausible, but target audience and guardian trust fit are unvalidated.

productFit.rationale: Initial size, cross-device layout, 16:9 behavior, incognito persistence, SDK events, and authentic thumbnails need substantial evidence.

trustSafety.rationale: Advertising, consent, SDK data, youth exposure, and player-experience implications require explicit review.

strategicLearning.rationale: Technical assessment can expose scale, performance, mobile, and integration constraints useful beyond one portal.

reachQuality.rationale: No Mythical-specific qualified reach, retention, or audience-quality evidence exists.

economicPotential.rationale: Revenue share, ads, fees, payout, implementation, support, and delivery economics are unverified.

controlRights.rationale: SDK, advertising, exclusivity, updates, assets, data, removal, and derivatives require terms review.

integrationEffort.rationale: Size, asset, device, aspect, persistence, SDK, event, and QA requirements create the largest current integration burden.

operationalLoad.rationale: Ongoing QA, updates, incidents, support, advertising, data, and reporting lack owners and cost evidence.

reversibility.rationale: An isolated adapter may preserve the core build, but SDK and platform dependencies increase exit work.

assessments.internalNextAction: Keep fourth in sequence; test its hardest size/device/SDK constraints during GDH-005 without creating an account, accepting terms, or integrating the SDK.
